A1.justification: Both readable ten-page PDFs clearly describe successive versions of the same work, renamed from HandSplat to HandSCS. Neither contains an appendix. v2 refers camera specifications, implementation details and additional comparisons to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF, limiting those checks; the visible scientific changes remain assessable.

before.justification: v1 reports original InterHand2.6M rendering experiments, speed measurements and component ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original novel-pose and novel-view rendering experiments and structural-component ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–7.

M1.justification: v2 adds Structural Coordinate Space: modified skeletal connectivity, learned dynamic bones and angular–radial descriptors supplied to Gaussian attribute decoders. It retains separate geometry/appearance embeddings and EMA-based consistency, but extends regularization to feature vectors and changes the pose-similarity decay from trainable to fixed at 1.5. These are substantive procedural changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three InterHand2.6M right-hand subjects and ROM03/04/07 sequences. v2 adds held-out novel-view synthesis alongside novel-pose animation, substantially extending evaluation from unseen articulations to unseen camera viewpoints.

E2.justification: The overall comparator set remains LiveHand, HandAvatar and GauHuman. However, v1 evaluates HandAvatar in a separate split-specific comparison, whereas v2 includes it alongside the others in the main novel-pose comparison. This changes reported comparator participation without establishing matched splits. GaussianHand and 3D-PSHR remain excluded.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct novel-view protocol using 10 training views and 15 held-out test views. The novel-pose last-50-frames test rule and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics remain. v1's explicit HandAvatar-specific split exception disappears from v2, leaving its revised evaluation setting insufficiently specified rather than demonstrating a confirmed common-split rerun.

E4.justification: v1 ablates Gaussian-Embedded Correction, pose-conditioned regularization and local-aware densification. v2 replaces this with embedding/inter-pose/intra-pose comparisons and adds separate static-versus-dynamic bone and interpolation-versus-offset ablations (Tables 2–4, Figures 6–7). These investigate new structural mechanisms; the dedicated densification ablation is no longer reported.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Both present point estimates; additional subjects and result rows in v2 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised and expanded. For test/Capture0 novel poses, the proposed method's PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS changes from 33.04/0.964/0.0338 to 32.91/0.966/0.0291; GauHuman PSNR changes from 32.29 to 31.71, while LiveHand's scores remain unchanged. v2 adds novel-view and structural-ablation results. Its teaser reports 58 FPS versus v1 Table 1's 66 FPS, without established hardware comparability. HandAvatar's changed scores cannot be interpreted as same-split improvements.

T1.justification: v2 introduces substantial mathematical definitions for hybrid bone topology, attention-smoothed dynamic endpoints and angular–radial structural coordinates (Equations 1–7), absent from v1. It also revises the consistency objective's attribute set. Conversely, v1's explicit EMA contribution derivation and local densification equations are no longer presented. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on disentangled embeddings, pose-conditioned regularization and local gradient-aware densification. v2 redefines the central contribution as explicit intra-pose and inter-pose structural guidance, particularly Structural Coordinate Space with hybrid bones. High-fidelity real-time animation remains a shared claim, but the principal novelty and supporting scientific argument change substantially.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of static bones providing global structural stability and dynamic bones providing local flexibility, including possible pose errors from unconstrained dynamic bones. It interprets LiveHand's novel-view SSIM advantage through smoother interpolation and explicitly identifies inaccurate MANO initialization as a persistent failure condition. These extend and redirect v1's embedding, temporal-consistency and densification interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies two 256-unit decoder hidden layers, zero-initialized output gates, 778-vertex initialization, random color/opacity initialization, A100 timing hardware and additional parameter values. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit densification procedure and embedding-smoothing formula with k=20 and weight scale 2000, although related components remain mentioned. Code release remains deferred; further implementation details are assigned to unavailable supplementary material.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands and revises research positioning around missing explicit structural guidance in prior Gaussian avatars. It adds discussion or citations including AMVUR, PHRIT, SplattingAvatar and GoMAvatar, while dropping works including JGHand and InterHandGS. The novelty argument shifts from improved embeddings and densification toward bone-relative structural coordinates.

P1.justification: Beyond the HandSplat-to-HandSCS title and terminology change, the abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work expands from two subsections to four, and the method and experiments are reorganized around structural guidance, implementation details and separate rendering tasks.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework diagram, adds a Structural Coordinate Space illustration, reorganizes qualitative comparison panels and adds novel-view and coordinate-basis visuals. Table 1 becomes a two-task comparison without the FPS column, and the ablation displays expand into Tables 2–4. These substantially change the visual presentation, beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more diagnostic evidence through held-out-view testing and separate structural-component ablations, and adds a concrete MANO-initialization limitation. These improve support and qualification beyond v1's single component-ablation study. Benefits are tempered by lost HandAvatar split clarity, removal of comparative FPS results and omitted implementation details. Moreover, v2 calls GauHuman the strongest novel-view baseline despite HandAvatar's higher average PSNR and LiveHand's higher average SSIM in Table 1, limiting confidence in its comparative interpretation.
